title: A Survey on Integration of Network Communication into Vehicle Real-Time Motion Control
domain: Vehicular real-time motion control with in-vehicle and V2X communications

analysis_policy.exclude_scope: References, author bios/photos, acknowledgments, appendix, nomenclature
analysis_policy.notes: Stop before references; span tags kept as headings markers.

section_flow.objective: Motivate integrating communication into vehicle real-time motion control, position gap vs prior surveys, and state contributions with roadmap.
key_components: Need for closed-loop control with communication uncertainty
Prior survey comparison and identified gap
notable_moves: Early related-work subsection with table-style comparison to underline novelty

evidence_locators.claim: States gap: few surveys tie communication impairments directly to vehicle real-time control loops.

raw_headings: II. ARCHITECTURE OF CONTROL OVER COMMUNICATIONS
section_flow.objective: Present high-level architecture linking control loops with communication networks.
key_components: Control system blocks and communication links
notable_moves: Uses architecture figure to anchor subsequent sections

evidence_locators.claim: Describes architecture integrating control blocks with networks.

locator.heading: II. ARCHITECTURE OF CONTROL OVER COMMUNICATIONS

notable_moves: Splits intra/inter-vehicle tech then reunifies in architecture discussion
Includes a discussion subsection to surface gaps

evidence_locators.claim: Covers intra-vehicle buses and inter-vehicle networks before architecture synthesis.

key_components: Communication delay/loss modeling in each domain
notable_moves: Uses repeated domain subsections followed by a discussion to consolidate lessons

evidence_locators.claim: Treats each control domain with attention to communication effects and ends with discussion.

notable_moves: Challenge subsections mirror prior taxonomy (intra, inter, integrated, realism)

locator.heading: VII. OPEN PROBLEMS AND FUTURE CHALLENGES

section_flow.objective: Recap survey scope and restate future integration needs.
notable_moves: Concise wrap-up that points back to integration agenda

evidence_locators.claim: Restates contributions and need for tighter control-communication integration.

hook.evidence: Notes emerging real-time vehicle control demands and communication unreliability risks.

gap.evidence: States lack of surveys coupling communication characteristics with vehicle control design.

yes_but.evidence: Existing works cover networking or control separately but not integrated real-time co-design.

organization.evidence: Outlines paper structure at the end of intro.

scope_boundary.evidence: Focuses on intra-vehicle, inter-vehicle, and integrated control under communication constraints.

rhetorical_moves_global.reader_contract_pattern: Motivate real-time control need; compare surveys; present architecture; cover intra/inter control with discussions; integrate streams; list challenges; conclude.

visuals_tables.layout_logic: Intro and architecture sections rely on figures to orient control-network interactions; technology and control sections interleave figures per subsection and end with discussion blocks; tables summarize comparisons of network technologies or architectures.

figures.purpose: show control over communications reference model

lesson_blocks.lesson: Split intra vs inter-vehicle networks, then reunify in an architecture discussion to expose integration gaps.
For each control domain, present communication constraints and end with a discussion subsection.
Contrast distributed vs centralized schemes and distill trade-offs in a closing discussion.
Map open problems to the same intra/inter/integrated taxonomy and add realism/simulation gap.

synthesis.aha_moment: Repeating a pattern of subsection deep dives followed by explicit discussions keeps technical breadth digestible and aligns challenges to the same structure.

style.section_openers_pattern: Open sections by framing the control or communication problem, then drill into subcases before a discussion block.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Intro gap with related-survey mini-section
steps: State the real-time control problem and why communication imperfections matter.
Insert a short related-survey comparison to surface the integration gap.
List contributions and outline the paper.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Gap evidence is shown immediately via comparison, building credibility before deep dives.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Architecture anchor before technology survey
steps: Present an architecture figure showing control blocks and communication links.
Describe timing/reliability needs at a high level.
Use this reference model to motivate the next technology survey section.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Gives readers a scaffold to hang diverse technologies on, improving coherence.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Subsection-deep-dive plus discussion pattern
steps: For each theme (e.g., powertrain, chassis, distributed control), first describe mechanism and communication constraints.
After covering all subthemes, add a short discussion subsection to surface trade-offs and gaps.
Repeat the pattern in later sections for consistency.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Creates a predictable rhythm and compresses takeaways after detailed coverage.

reusable_writing_recipes.title: Challenges mapped to taxonomy with realism add-on
steps: List challenges per previously used taxonomy (intra, inter, integrated).
Add cross-cutting issues like simulation-to-reality gaps and nonideal comms.
reusable_writing_recipes.why_it_works: Maintains continuity with earlier structure and highlights actionable future work.

notes: Equation count heuristic triggered by inline markers; adjust if needed. Headings contain span markers from conversion.
